title: Events: why the Market Calendar matters to sellers
summary: Results gaps, IV crush, dividends and corporate actions, market-wide events, and how to use the Market Calendar.

questions.q: Why can't a stop-loss protect a short option through a results gap?
options: Stop-losses are disabled on results day
The price jumps overnight, past the stop, before any trade can happen
questions.why: The first trade after the gap is already beyond the stop level.

questions.q: Implied volatility usually does what after results are announced?
questions.why: The uncertainty is resolved, so IV and premiums fall.

questions.q: A dividend record date before expiry is mainly a risk for:
options: Short calls close to the money
questions.why: An ITM or near-ITM call may be exercised early to capture the dividend.

questions.q: After a stock split, your option contract's strike and lot size:
options: Are adjusted, keeping the position's value equivalent
questions.why: The exchange adjusts the contract so the position's value is unchanged.

questions.q: You hold a strangle and results are announced for next week, before expiry. The best time to decide what to do is:
questions.why: Decide calmly before the event, not during a gap.
